experiment: An explicit next-piece loss: at every encoder frame the model must name the BPE piece that comes next, from the audio so far and the token history
motivation: In context_fusion_v1 the long-context decoder branch was trained with the transducer loss and the delay penalty only. No loss ever asked the model for the next piece before the transducer emits it: the transducer loss trains the token distribution where the alignment emits, and blank everywhere else. Only the text-only LM had a next-piece loss, and it names the first piece of the next word 19% of the time. This experiment adds that loss on audio plus token context and tests whether the predictions speed up the display.
head: Next-piece classifier on one encoder frame (256) and the decoder output (512, including the long-context branch when present): own projections to 512, tanh, 500 classes; class 0 means that nothing follows. 0.65M parameters
loss: Sum over frames t and states u of py[u,t] * cross-entropy(head(encoder frame t, decoder state u), piece u+1). py is the occupation of the blank arcs of the simple lattice (already computed for pruning): the probability that the alignment leaves frame t with u pieces emitted. Each valid frame carries total weight 1. Evaluated on the pruned band of 5 states. Added to the RNN-T loss with a weight
use_at_display: After every zero-fill preview pass the head, read at the newest encoder frame that holds real audio and chained through the decoder state, proposes up to two further pieces. They are appended to the preview tokens and pass through the same display gate (study `ant`). Study `hq` gives the gate the head's probability of each transducer preview token instead. Study `free` is the gate of emit_early_v1 and context_fusion_v1

arms.joint_480min: 960h, SpecAugment, lr 0.0005 with linear decay to 10%, 160/320ms training chunks, averaged weights, 480 minutes on a V100, from the public 20M model: np_w02_dp010 (weight 0.02, penalty 0.01), np_w10_dp010 (0.1, 0.01), np_w02_dp005 (0.02, 0.005), np_ctx_w02_dp010 (long-context branch of context_fusion_v1 design D, 0.02, 0.01). Head and branch parameters use AdamW (head lr 0.001)
arms.probe_90min: Head only, recognizer frozen and run as in decoding (320ms chunks, no dropout, no SpecAugment): np_probe_dp010 on emit_early_v1 r4_dp010_sc_decay (ema), np_probe_ctx_dp010 on context_fusion_v1 cf_ctx480_dp010 (ema). Final output and WER are those of the frozen model
arms.matched_baselines: emit_early_v1 r4_dp010_sc_decay and r4_dp005_sc_decay, context_fusion_v1 cf_ctx480_dp010 (all 480 minutes, same recipe without the loss)

hypotheses.H1: Display: on np_w02_dp010 the anticipated pieces lower the R1 delay of the gated display by at least 10ms on dev-clean and on dev-other against the same model's gate without them (`ant` against `free`)
hypotheses.H2: No retraining needed: the same gain of at least 10ms at R1 appears on the frozen penalty-0.01 baseline (np_probe_dp010)
hypotheses.H3: Recognizer: the loss makes the recognizer itself earlier. At 480 minutes the joint arms with weight 0.02 have at least 10ms less word delay without previews than their matched baselines, at a full-dev WER that is not higher (the paired interval does not lie above zero), at both penalties
hypotheses.H4: Predictability: after a chunk's native pass (all audio real, no lookahead) the head names the next piece correctly at least 10 points more often than the external LM and than the transducer's best non-blank piece, over 1,500 dev utterances (np_w02_dp010)
hypotheses.H5: Token context adds to audio: with the long-context branch the head's accuracy at word starts is at least 5 points higher than without it (np_ctx_w02_dp010 against np_w02_dp010)

evaluation: As in context_fusion_v1: eight zero-fill previews per 320ms chunk, hold display, gate fitted on 800 dev utterances and thresholds chosen on 300 others, delay and rewrites on the fixed 200 + 200 subset, WER on all of dev-clean and dev-other with a paired utterance bootstrap against the matched baseline; every encoder pass charged 5.0ms, head and LM steps not charged; test unused. Next-piece accuracy is measured on the 1,500 dev utterances of the gate (fit, selection and evaluation sets) against the model's own final output
known_limits_before_running: The head is trained on ordinary chunked passes, where a frame sees real audio up to the end of its chunk, and is used on zero-fill previews, where the rest of the chunk is zero. Weights 0.02 and 0.1 are guesses: per frame the next-piece loss is roughly 50 times the RNN-T loss. One run per arm, one seed. Wall-clock budgets do not equalise step counts
compute: USC CARC Discovery, one GPU per job; two 3-4 minute smoke jobs run first and every long job waits for both to succeed
